content.text:
**Finding: compliant (preferred position) — no redline proposed.**

Investigation covered every plausible location for a restrictive covenant:

| Location | Result |
|---|---|
| §12 Customer Responsibilities | **§12.3 affirmatively disclaims** any exclusivity, non-compete, MFC, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment, and confirms we may develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product or service in any field or territory |
| §12.4 | Restriction runs **against Vendor** (no competing analytics service during the term) — benefits us, not flagged |
| §13 Licence / §13.4 | Only Customer-side restrictions are standard anti-reverse-engineering, anti-interference and lawful-use terms, expressly carved back for authorized security testing and use of Customer Data — not a non-compete or field-of-use limit |
| §2 Scope | §2.1 confirms no minimum quantity or purchase commitment; a decision not to order again is not a breach |
| §§14, 16, 9–11, 24, 25, 30 | Searches for "compet*", "exclusiv*/field of use/territory", "Customer shall not", "restrict/refrain/agrees not to", "develop", "similar/solicit/hire", and "for a period of/months after/know-how/benchmark" surfaced no covenant binding our business, products or purchasing, and no post-term restriction of any kind |

Because the single preferred element is already met on the document's face, the fallback checklist (named product, term-only, 12-month cap, internal-development and acquisition carve-outs) is not engaged. Nothing here requires narrowing, and I did not flag the Vendor-side covenant in §12.4, which is a protection in our favour.
